about.title: Redwood City Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Patients in Redwood City expect care that meets a professional standard. Most of the time that is exactly what happens. Sometimes, though, a diagnosis is missed, a medication is mixed up, or a surgery goes wrong in a way that careful practice would have avoided. California law calls that medical negligence, and it is different from simply having a bad result — a poor outcome by itself is not malpractice. San Mateo County residents also face a specific set of rules under MICRA. You generally have one year from the date you discovered the harm to file, and never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit begins. Non-economic damages are capped at a figure that rises every year, and nearly every case needs a qualified medical expert to explain what should have happened. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Redwood City patients with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement. The attorney we connect you with can track those dates from your first call.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built In
items.desc: Almost every California malpractice claim needs a qualified medical expert to confirm the standard of care was breached. Attorneys in our network know how to arrange that review early, before a deadline becomes a problem.

items.title: Honest About the Cap
items.desc: MICRA limits non-economic damages, and that limit rises each year. An independent attorney can explain how the current figure applies to your situation without overstating what a claim can do.

items.question: I was injured in a collision on US-101 near Redwood City and then received poor care afterward. Do I have two separate claims?
items.answer: Possibly. Redwood City recorded 305 injury collisions in 2025, and many of those patients were treated at local hospitals. A crash claim against another driver and a malpractice claim against a provider are handled under different rules, including MICRA's shorter deadlines and expert requirement for the medical side. An attorney can review whether both are worth pursuing.

items.question: My surgery did not turn out the way I hoped. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law distinguishes between a disappointing result and a provider who fell below the accepted standard of care. A qualified medical expert usually has to review your records to make that determination. That review is a normal first step, and the attorney you are connected with can arrange it.

items.question: How does the 90-day notice work in San Mateo County?
items.answer: Before a malpractice lawsuit is filed anywhere in California, including San Mateo County, the provider must receive written notice of intent at least 90 days ahead. That notice can affect how the filing deadline is calculated. Because timing matters, it is worth speaking with an attorney as soon as you suspect something went wrong.
